solutionTimeAttendance.title: Time attendance that feeds payroll.
solutionTimeAttendance.lead: Face, fingerprint and card terminals record when people arrive and leave. BioTime turns each punch into a timesheet your payroll team can export.

story.heading: From a punch to a payroll file.

story.label: How time attendance works
story.alt: An attendance terminal sends check-ins to BioTime, which builds a timesheet and exports it for payroll

steps.title: Check in at the terminal
steps.body: A face, fingerprint or card verifies the person. The terminal stores the punch with the time.

steps.title: Punches reach BioTime
steps.body: Over the network, Wi-Fi or 4G, depending on the model, punches arrive in BioTime on your server or in the cloud.

steps.title: Timesheets build themselves
steps.body: BioTime matches punches to shifts and fills each person's day: in, out and hours worked.

steps.title: Export for payroll
steps.body: Approved timesheets are exported as a file for your payroll or HR system.

software.lead: ZKTeco attendance software, from one office to many sites. Confirm which version fits your terminals with AIMS.
software.purposeOnPremise: Attendance and workforce management, installed on your own server.
software.purposeCloud: Cloud-based attendance and workforce management for one or many sites.
software.purposeMobile: Staff and managers see attendance and reports on a phone.

items.q: How many terminals do I need?
items.a: Usually one per entrance staff use at shift change. Large teams may need more so queues stay short. AIMS will suggest a number from your headcount and entrances.

items.q: Face, fingerprint or card: which is best?
items.a: Face is touch-free and fast. Fingerprint has a low cost per person. Cards are familiar but can be lent, so many sites pair them with face or fingerprint.

items.q: Can I use one system for several sites?
items.a: Yes. BioTime Cloud, or BioTime on a server your sites can reach, collects punches from terminals in different locations.

items.q: Can terminals also open a door?
items.a: Some models support access control as well as attendance. Check the model's specifications, or ask AIMS about the lock and exit button it needs.

items.q: Does it work with my payroll software?
items.a: BioTime exports attendance reports as files. Share your payroll system with AIMS to confirm the format before you order.

cta.heading: Plan attendance for your site.
cta.body: Tell AIMS how many people and entrances you have. You'll get a device plan and a quotation.

solutionAccessControl.title: Decide who opens every door.
solutionAccessControl.lead: Readers, controllers, locks and software for one door or a whole building. AIMS supplies, installs and sets them up across the UAE.

door.heading: Six parts at every controlled door.
door.lead: Tap a card: the reader reads it, the controller checks it and the lock releases. Each part is a model in the AIMS catalogue.
door.partsLabel: The six parts of a controlled door

parts.reader: Reads the card at the door and passes it to the controller.
parts.controller: Decides who may enter, and when. InBio Pro panels run one, two or four doors.
parts.lock: Holds the door shut with 280 kg and releases when access is granted.
parts.exit: Lets people leave from the inside without a card.
parts.card: The credential each person taps at the reader.
parts.software: Add users, set door permissions and watch door events live.

methods.heading: Choose how people prove who they are.
methods.lead: Start with the method that suits each door. Counts are access control products in the AIMS catalogue.

card.title: Card
card.body: The simplest to roll out. A lost card is removed in the software.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.body: Checks the person, not only what they carry. Nothing to lend or lose.

face.title: Face
face.body: Touch-free at busy doors. Some models also read a card or a palm.

palm.title: Palm
palm.body: Touch-free palm reading, on terminals that also recognise faces.

products.heading: Panels and terminals to start with.
products.lead: Panels for one, two and four doors, and terminals for each method. Add the ones you want, with quantities, to your quote.

software.lead: Run doors from one Windows PC or from a browser. Confirm with AIMS which version fits your panels.

software.purposeCvaccess: Web-based access control for devices and doors across several locations.
software.purposeCvsecurity: One web platform for access control, visitors, parking and video.

items.q: Can one panel run more than one door?
items.a: Yes. The InBio Pro 160 controls one door, the 260 two and the 460 four, according to their specifications. Larger sites use more panels.

items.q: Card, fingerprint or face: which is best?
items.a: A card is the simplest. Fingerprint, face and palm terminals check the person, not only the card. AIMS helps you choose for each door.

items.q: Can I keep my existing readers?
items.a: InBio Pro panels take 26-bit Wiegand and RS485 FR series readers. Send AIMS your reader's model to check.

items.q: Which lock suits my door?
items.a: The AL-M280 electromagnetic lock holds 280 kg and is listed for wooden, glass, metal and fireproof doors. AIMS checks your doors on the site survey.

items.q: Can a terminal open the door by itself?
items.a: Some can. The F18 and SpeedFace V5L-P list a lock, door sensor and exit button connection in their specifications. Check the model, or ask AIMS.

cta.heading: Plan access for your doors.

solutionEntranceParking.title: Turnstiles for lobbies, barriers for car parks.
solutionEntranceParking.lead: Turnstiles and swing or flap barriers decide who walks in. Barrier gates, plate recognition and radar sensors manage the cars.

lanes.heading: One credential, one lane open.
lanes.lead: What happens at a lane, for people and for cars.
lanes.alt: A reader checks a card and a swing barrier opens; a camera reads a number plate and a boom barrier lifts

steps.title: Present a credential
steps.body: A card, fingerprint, QR code or face at the reader. Some turnstiles come with the reader built in.

steps.title: The barrier opens
steps.body: Flaps retract, arms swing or the tripod turns, and sensors watch for anyone following too close.

steps.title: Cars read by plate
steps.body: A plate recognition camera reads the number plate and tells the barrier gate to lift.

steps.title: Safe in an emergency
steps.body: On many models the barriers open or the arms drop in an emergency or power cut.

tripod.body: A compact lane where a rotating tripod lets people through. Arms drop in a power cut on models such as TS1200 and TS2100.

speed.title: Flap or swing barrier
speed.body: Faster lanes for busy lobbies. The FBL5000 lists up to 30 people a minute; flaps open in an emergency.

full.title: Full-height turnstile
full.body: Floor-to-head lanes where security matters most. The FHT2300 lists security level High.

vehicle.title: Parking barrier
vehicle.body: Boom barriers from 3 m to 6 m, with plate recognition and radar sensors for car parks.

software.purposeCvsecurity: Access control, visitors, and parking and vehicle control in one web platform.

items.q: Can a turnstile come with its own reader?
items.a: Some do. The TS1022 Pro comes with a controller and a fingerprint and RFID reader, and the FBL4000, FBL4200 and SBT1000S ship with the card or fingerprint reader you choose. Others take readers you add.

items.q: What happens in a power cut?
items.a: On flap barriers such as the FBL4000 and FBL5000 the barriers retract when a battery is installed, and on tripods such as the TS1200 and TS2100 the arms drop, so people can leave.

items.q: Tripod, flap, swing or full height?
items.a: Full-height turnstiles suit high-security entrances. Flap and swing barriers move more people: the FBL5000 lists up to 30 a minute. Tripods are compact. AIMS helps you choose for each entrance.

items.q: Can a barrier open by number plate?
items.a: Yes. The LPRC100 camera and the LPRS4000 system read number plates and connect to barrier gates. The VR10 radar detects cars and people at the barrier without cutting the road for a loop.

items.q: Do you supply security screening?
items.a: Yes: ZK-D180 and ZK-D100S handheld metal detectors, the ZK-D3180S metal detector with 18 detection zones, and the ZKX5030A X-ray system for bags and parcels.

items.q: Smart lock or hotel lock?
items.a: Smart locks such as the TL700 open by fingerprint, password or card, for homes and offices. Hotel locks such as the LH4000 open with RFID key cards and are built for guest rooms.

items.q: Do you have a lock for glass doors?
items.a: Yes. The GL300 opens by fingerprint, MF card, password or remote control, clamps on without drilling and fits 10–12 mm glass.

items.q: Which locks work with a phone?
items.a: The TL800, TL700W, TL300 and HBL400 connect over Wi-Fi. The TL800 and TL700W use the ZSmart app to open the door remotely, share temporary passwords and see the lock's records.

items.q: What if the batteries run out?
items.a: The locks warn you first. The TL700, TL800 and GL300 have a micro-USB emergency power port; the AL20DB and TL400 take a 9V battery for emergency power.

items.q: How are hotel locks managed?
items.a: With hotel lock software: the LH4000 lists ZKBiolock, and the LH6000 and LH6500 also list ZKBioSecurity. The CR60W is a USB RFID reader for hotel management. Confirm the software version with AIMS.

cta.heading: Plan locks for your doors.
cta.body: Tell AIMS which doors, rooms and users you have. You'll get a lock plan and a quotation.

items.q: Will my POS software run on it?
items.a: Choose by the software you run: Windows terminals for Windows POS software, Android terminals for Android apps. Share your software's requirements with AIMS before you order.

items.q: Is there a POS with a fingerprint reader?
items.a: Yes. The ZKBio900 series (ZKBio910, ZKBio930 and ZKBio950) has built-in fingerprint verification for staff.

items.q: Which terminals print receipts?
items.a: The ZKAIO1000 and ZKH300 have a 58 mm thermal printer built in. Other terminals pair with a printer such as the ZKP8001, which has an auto cutter.

items.q: Is there a handheld POS?
items.a: Yes. The ZKH300 has a 5.5-inch touchscreen, 4G, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, a 5600 mAh battery and a camera that scans barcodes and QR codes.

items.q: Can customers see the total?
items.a: Yes, on a customer display: an LED digit display on the ZK15, ZK1515, ZKBio900 and ZKAIO1000, and a 4.3-inch LCD option on the ZKAIO1000.

story: AIMS Security Systems Trading LLC distributes and installs ZKTeco security products across the UAE: attendance terminals, access control readers and panels, turnstiles and barriers, smart and hotel locks, and POS hardware.
Its team covers sales, sales engineering and after-sales technical support, so the people who quote a system can also install it and look after it.
AIMS works from a head office and a showroom in Deira, Dubai, and an office in Abu Dhabi, and fills project and export orders for GCC countries and East Africa.
